🌍 World Map Maker

"Here be dragons. Also here. And, regrettably, here."

Draw your own fantasy world map: paint the land and the coast draws itself, color its forests, deserts, and snowfields, then drag and drop towns, castles, mountains, ships, and sea monsters onto it. Draw borders, roads, and rivers, and name it all in the old fonts. Everything saves in your browser as you draw.

🏝️ Land and sea

Paint land and the coast draws itself. Right-click or hold Shift to paint sea back: bays, lakes, and channels.

🎲 Start from random land

New land replaces the old (and with terrain, the terrain symbols). Your places, labels, and lines stay. Undo brings the old land back.

🌳 Terrain colors

A wash of color over the land, never the sea. Right-click or hold Shift to wipe it back to plain land. For mountains and trees themselves, use 🏰 Icons.

🏰 Icons

Drag an icon onto the map, or click one and then click the map (keep the button down to slide it into place). Terrain symbols overlap the right way, lower over higher. R turns the next one 15° before it goes down (Shift+R the other way). Move, resize, turn, or flip any icon with 👆 Select.

✒️ Borders, roads, and rivers

Click to put down points and double-click (or press Enter) to finish, or drag to draw freehand. Click the first point to close a shape. Backspace takes back a point, Esc stops.

Then change its color, width, and dashes, or fill a region, in the panel below.

🔤 Text

Click the map (or drag a style onto it) and type. Change the font, size, color, halo, spacing, curve, and turn below; R turns the next label 15° before it goes down. Double-click a label with 👆 Select to type in it again.

🧽 Erase

Drag over icons and labels to rub them out, or click a line. To take away land, paint sea with 🏝️ Land.

📏 Ruler

Drag from one place to another for the miles between them, and the days it takes on foot (24 miles a day). Set how many miles the map is across under 🎨 Colors, coast, frame, and grid.

✋ Pan

Drag to move around the map. With any tool, hold Space or the middle mouse button and drag. Ctrl + mouse wheel zooms.

🗺️ Take it to the table

Your maps are kept in this browser only, up to 30 of them, saved as you draw (💾 Back up everything). 🔗 Copy Link puts the whole map in the link, so whoever opens it gets their own copy to change. Want a whole continent rolled for you, with nations, rulers, and roads? Try the Worldbuilder's Continent Map Generator. The icons, textures, and frame are the Gazette's own.

How the World Map Maker works

Paint the land with a brush and the coastline draws itself, with shallows around it. Wash the land with terrain colors, then drag and drop the icons: towns and capitals, ruins and towers, mountains, forests, and dunes, ships and sea monsters, a compass rose, and coats of arms in your own colors. Draw borders, roads, rivers, and regions, and label it all. 🎨 Illustrated paints the parchment and sea; 📜 Parchment ink and 🌑 Dark draw flat colors you can change.

Tools

  • 🏝️ Land (B): paint land or sea, or roll random land (one continent, two, scattered islands, or a coast) to start from, with its terrain filled in.
  • 🌳 Terrain (G): forest, jungle, grassland, desert, badlands, swamp, snow, and tundra.
  • 🏰 Icons (I): drag them onto the map, or scatter terrain symbols with a stroke of the brush.
  • ✒️ Lines (L): borders, roads, trails, rivers, sea routes, walls, and regions you can fill. Any line can be solid, dashed, or dotted, in any color and width, smooth or straight, with a soft band along it.
  • 🔤 Text (T): realm, region, sea, and town names in Cinzel, IM Fell, Lato, or Georgia, with a halo to read over busy ground, spaced out, and curved.
  • 👆 Select (V): move, resize, turn, flip, duplicate, or delete anything; drag a line's points to reshape it.
  • 🧽 Erase (E), 📏 Ruler (M), and ✋ Pan (H). Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.

For the whole map

  • Under 🎨 Colors, coast, frame, and grid: the sea, land, and coast colors, how thick and how rugged the coastline is, the shallows, a vine border or a plain one, a hex or square grid for overland travel, and a scale bar.
  • Set how many miles the map is across, and the ruler and the scale bar count in miles.

Works with

Its other half, the Battlemap Builder, draws the fights on a 5-foot grid. Plan the trip with the Travel & Weather Generator, and pin notes on any map with the Worldbuilder's Your Maps tab (download the PNG, then upload it there).
